items.title: OpenAI may be in cost control mode (2 minute read)
items.snippet: OpenAI's Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 updates received criticism for reduced performance, as both models show significant reductions in reasoning and output tokens. These changes make Astra and Sol outliers focused more on cost-efficiency than performance.

items.title: LayerStream: faster MoE fine-tuning on fewer or cheaper GPUs (10 minute read)
items.snippet: Nebius' LayerStream training engine keeps optimizer state and saved activations in host memory and streams each layer's working state through the GPU only when that layer runs. On 16 H200 GPUs, it finished a pass over a 25.8M-token dataset in 7.1 minutes instead of 22.4, with 3.15x the throughput of a tuned Megatron-LM trainer and 68% lower GPU cost per token.

items.title: Do scale-dependent algorithms cut against a software intelligence explosion? (13 minute read)
items.snippet: Scale-dependent algorithms will cut against a software-only intelligence explosion. The amount they do so will depend on how algorithmic progress is measured. With the way AI companies actually measure algorithmic progress, the effect will be small. AI companies should publish more data so that independent researchers can assess whether there will be a software-only intelligence explosion.
